answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated results or duplicate identities. Because rewards are weighted by verified contribution rather than account count, splitting one operator across many identities brings no extra influence; each new identity needs more capital and risks losing it. The delta sets the stake dynamically: a tundra of cheap compute still cannot mint trust, and ivory credentials offer no exemption.
